_comment: darkmux profile registry — example. Four general-purpose reference profiles in increasing capacity order: fast → balanced → deep → gpt-oss, plus three review-pipeline-oriented reference profiles (devstral, qwen3.6-27b-review, judge-35b-moe — see `_review_staffing_comment` below), each a candidate for the review mission's single `reviewer` seat, plus one hosted endpoint example (hosted-frontier). A profile's `models[]` are WORKER models (no `role` field — #590); the machine's standing utility/compactor model lives once in the top-level `internal.utility` binding, not per-profile. `default_model` (optional) names a profile's default worker when it lists more than one; with a single model it's implicit. `n_ctx` is required for LOCAL models (it is the load parameter) and omitted for endpoint-bearing models (#1282). Replace the model ids with what you have downloaded in LMStudio (run `lms ls`).

fast.description: Single-turn tasks. Slim worker — fastest dispatch, lowest RAM.

balanced.description: Mid-range tasks. Predictable behavior across mixed workloads; compaction runs on the machine's internal.utility model.

deep.description: Long agentic tasks. Maximum worker context for fewer compactions.

gpt-oss.description: OpenAI gpt-oss-120b (MXFP4 quantization) for Apple Silicon — worker at 100K. Requires OpenClaw >= v2026.5.9-beta.1 (harmony format / tool-payload fix).

devstral.description: Review pipeline — a `reviewer`-role candidate (`darkmux config set role_profiles.reviewer devstral`). Dense wide-instruct model, no reasoning trace. (#2169) The observed case this issue was filed for was `mistralai/devstral-small-2-2512` — a DIFFERENT id from the `devstral-small-2507` pinned below; whether 2507 shares the same LM Studio Mistral-parser interaction (structured tool_calls whose `name` is model content sliced around its own [TOOL_CALLS] marker) is unconfirmed. Either way darkmux never executes a call like that regardless of which Devstral id produced it — partitioned + coalesced via the `malformed_tool_names` detector rather than dispatched. Not a reason to avoid this profile; worth knowing if that detector fires in a run's telemetry.

qwen3.6-27b-review.description: Review pipeline — a second `reviewer`-role candidate, a distinct dense wide-instruct model, useful for A/B-ing the seat against `devstral` (the shipped `review` mission has one `reviewer` seat, reused across every rule — not parallel probes).

judge-35b-moe.description: Review pipeline — a third `reviewer`-role candidate: an MoE reasoner, for when the review unit benefits from a reasoning trace rather than the dense wide-instruct models above. (#2310 P4d retired the dedicated judge stage this profile originally staffed; it's now just another candidate for the single `reviewer` seat, same as the two above.)

hosted-frontier.description: Hosted (endpoint-bearing) model — declares NO n_ctx: the provider owns the context window, so there is no local load parameter to invent (#1282). No `auth` block here either: a placeholder credential source would make a fresh `darkmux init` fail doctor's credentials check spuriously. When your endpoint needs credentials, add an `auth` block naming a credential SOURCE — either `"auth": { "type": "api-key", "keychain": "<item-name>" }` (a macOS Keychain ITEM name, never the secret itself) or `"auth": { "type": "api-key", "key_env": "AZURE_OPENAI_KEY" }` (#1312 — the NAME of an env var holding the key, for ANY provider: `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `AZURE_OPENAI_KEY`, anything). You can declare BOTH — `"auth": { "type": "api-key", "keychain": "darkmux-azure-example", "key_env": "AZURE_OPENAI_KEY" }` — and the env var WINS when it is present in the environment: `security` is never read, so a headless CI runner (export the var from its secret store) never touches a lockable login keychain. Neither `keychain` nor `key_env` ever holds the secret VALUE; only names. Replace the URL/deployment with your own, or delete this profile if you only run local models.

_review_staffing_comment: Review staffing is DERIVED via the role->profile flip (#1475), not declared. The shipped `review` mission config (#2310 P4d) has two dispatching roles, not five: `reviewer` (the per-unit `crawl.unit` dispatch that scans the diff for one rule — the same seat runs every rule, one dispatch per planned unit) and `coder` (the OPTIONAL `create-mod-dispatch` template, off by default, for an unattended runner writing a fix). Each resolves INDEPENDENTLY: a per-run launch override (`--param <role>=<profile>`) wins, else the machine-local `role_profiles` map in config.json (`darkmux config set role_profiles.<role> <profile>`), else `default_profile` (the fresh-user floor -- a bare machine runs every seat on one model). The three review-pipeline profiles above (devstral, qwen3.6-27b-review, judge-35b-moe) are reference candidates for the single `reviewer` seat, not roles darkmux resolves automatically — bind one: `darkmux config set role_profiles.reviewer devstral`. `coder` is shared with every other mission's coder seat (e.g. coder-phase); pin it globally, or scope the pin to just this mission's optional unattended path via `--param mod_seat_profile=<profile>` (`create-mod-dispatch`'s own override, read ahead of `role_profiles.coder`). A leftover `crews` key from a pre-2.0 file is harmless residue (`darkmux doctor` notes it).
